The appeal path, quoted from POL-GEN-04

Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

Escalation is terminal: no monetary outcome issues, so there is nothing for POL-GEN-05 to execute and the disputed amount is held rather than collected or refunded.

The judge's explanation, as written

To both parties: this dispute cannot be finally decided on the record as it stands, so it goes to a human reviewer and the $6.00 in dispute is held — neither collected nor refunded. The reason is an identifier mismatch. The fare breakdown in the bundle, EV-FARE-02834, is indexed to this trip, but the ledger's own record inside it says "trip_id": "TRP-02734", while the trip record EV-TRIP-02834 and the GPS trace EV-GPS-02834 both say TRP-02834. POL-RD-10(2) requires the trip identifiers on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown to all match and forbids a final ruling where they do not. The pre-pass marking the artifact COMPLETE does not answer this: POL-GEN-02(3) keeps the schema-level assessment separate from the policy-level test, and this is a policy-level test. So the rider's assertion that all three artifacts bear TRP-02834 holds for the trip record and the trace but not for the fare breakdown. What would resolve the case is a fare breakdown or payment-ledger export for TRP-02834 — a corrected ledger line, or the gantry/payment record for this trip; the reviewer can call for it. The rest of the record, so the reviewer has it. The deviation itself is established but not material: the trace measures 30.94 km against the booked optimal 23.8 km, an excess of 7.14 km (30.0%), which passes the POL-RD-01 gates of 0.8 km and 20% but is below the 8.0 km and 50% materiality marks, so no POL-RD-06 uplift and no conduct referral is available (the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 326 completed trips in 90 days in any event). The trace is not impaired for policy purposes — 243 fixes at 10 seconds, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 seconds — so POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10(3) are not engaged. Nothing exonerates the excess: the chat log is empty (POL-RD-04 and POL-RD-14 have no instruction to test), no pickup or dropoff was amended and no amended optimal exists (POL-RD-05), the vehicle is RYDE_X so the pooled baseline of POL-RD-12 does not apply, and the only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-02834-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and the driver's 'Followed navigation' statement — which names no advisory and asserts no closure, queue or incident — discharges nothing under POL-RD-08. That absence does not itself escalate the case: under POL-RD-13 the missing advisory is a gap in the bundle, not the cited-artifact defect POL-RD-10(5) describes, because the driver cited no advisory at all. The fare is metered (fare_model METERED, quoted_fare_sgd null), so POL-RD-11 does not apply and the POL-RD-02 arithmetic would run as charged_total 39.06 less recomputed_fare 31.4380 = 7.6220, rounding up to 7.65 — above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, below the 90% full-refund share, and below the SGD 150.00 escalation ceiling. The driver's argument that any award is capped at the $6.00 contested, and the rider's contrary arithmetic of 7.65, are noted for the reviewer; no money moves now, because escalation under POL-RD-10 is terminal. No referral is issued: no clause produces one here (no POL-RD-06(c) pattern; no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity defect, the ERP and surcharge lines all being zero). Confidence is 0.85, capped by the weight-1.0 artifacts that carry the deciding identifier facts. The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

What each side argued

The rider advocate

kept The governing distance figure is the trace, not the trip record. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km decisive where the two disagree, and forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test. The trace measures 30.94 km against a booked optimal of 23.8 km: an excess of 7.14 km, which is 30.0% of the optimal distance. Both establishment limbs pass on their face - the excess is greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20% - and the derived deviation block records the status as 'established'. The deviation is therefore ESTABLISHED for this trip.

evidence EV-GPS-02834, EV-TRIP-02834 · clauses POL-RD-01

kept The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged on the face of the artifacts. The three artifacts that carry the claim - trip record, GPS trace and fare breakdown - all bear trip identifier TRP-02834, and the trace runs from the trip record's own start (10:10:16) to its own completion (10:50:36) within the recorded window. The excess (7.14 km, 30.0%) is measured from a trace that is unimpaired, with 100% coverage, 243 fixes and no gaps. The burden therefore shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause for exoneration - a general assertion of good navigation does not discharge it.

evidence EV-TRIP-02834, EV-GPS-02834, EV-FARE-02834 · clauses POL-RD-08

kept No rider instruction can be pressed against this claim. POL-RD-04 exonerates a deviation only to the extent it is attributable to a rider instruction recorded in the chat_log and corroborated by the trace, and POL-RD-14 addresses only instructions that were made and not followed. The chat log for TRP-02834 carries zero messages (message_count 0, first and last message timestamps null), and the trip record's chat_message_count is likewise 0. There is no instruction in existence, so no distance is excluded on that ground and the deviation stands at its measured figure.

evidence EV-CHAT-02834, EV-TRIP-02834 · clauses POL-RD-04, POL-RD-14

kept The driver's statement that he 'Followed navigation' is an assertion of an external cause that reaches no artifact. The only traffic_advisory in the bundle is EV-ADVIS-02834-01, and that artifact is IMPAIRED TO THE POINT OF ABSENCE: admissibility status MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0, payload null, the pre-pass recording that no advisory covers the Northpoint City corridor in this window. I cite it for exactly that absence. Under POL-RD-13, POL-RD-03's comparison cannot be run on the record with no advisory covering the trip window, so POL-RD-03 is unavailable and the driver's excuse carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Because the driver names no evidence ID for any advisory, this is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, and it does not escalate the case under POL-RD-10(5).

evidence EV-ADVIS-02834-01, EV-GPS-02834 · clauses POL-RD-13, POL-RD-03, POL-RD-08

kept The trace is not impaired for policy purposes, so the rider's case does not depend on any corroborating source. POL-RD-07 impairs a trace only on a gap above 90 seconds, a straight-line jump above 500 m, or a sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds. This trace has a 10 second sample interval, max_gap_sec of 0.0, an empty gaps array and 100% coverage, so none of limbs (a) to (c) is met. The claim may rest on the trace alone, and the escalation route in POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

evidence EV-GPS-02834 · clauses POL-RD-07

kept The fare is metered, so the distance-and-time remedy is live. fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null. POL-RD-11 applies only where the fare model is UPFRONT_QUOTE with a non-null quoted fare, and it does not reach this trip; POL-RD-02 governs, and the rider's loss on distance and time is real rather than already absorbed at booking.

evidence EV-FARE-02834, EV-TRIP-02834 · clauses POL-RD-02, POL-RD-11

kept The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, run on the booked optimal route because no exoneration or adjustment clause applies. Charged_total is 39.06. Recomputed fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 23.8 km optimal + 0.28 x 32.1 min optimal) x the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier = 30.638, plus the 0.80 platform fee, plus zero ERP (no on-optimal-route gantry), plus no fixed surcharge, plus zero waiting time fee, less zero promo discount = 31.4380. Refund = 39.06 - 31.4380 = 7.6220, payable rounded up to SGD 7.65. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so no de minimis bar applies, and at 19.5% of charged_total it does not reach the 90% full-refund share, so the correct outcome on these lines is PARTIAL_REFUND. The computed figure of 7.65 exceeds the SGD 6.00 the rider put in issue, so the claim is made out in full and then some.

evidence EV-FARE-02834, EV-TRIP-02834 · clauses POL-RD-02

The driver advocate

kept The only distance figure POL-RD-01 allows for the threshold test is the trace figure: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 30.94 km against a booked optimal of 23.8 km, so the excess is 7.14 km and 30.0% (trip_record.actual_distance_km, 30.9, is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and may not be cited). That excess clears the establishment gate of 0.8 km and 20%, but it fails BOTH materiality limbs: 7.14 km is under the 8.0 km absolute figure and 30.0% is under the 50% proportional figure. This is therefore at most an ordinary established deviation; it cannot be uplifted to a FULL_REFUND of charged_total under POL-RD-06(b) and it cannot generate a POL-RD-06(c) driver-conduct referral.

evidence EV-GPS-02834, EV-TRIP-02834 · clauses POL-RD-01, POL-RD-06

kept No repeat-deviation pattern is established on the driver's own numbers: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 326, a ratio of 0.000, far below the 0.05 test POL-RD-06 sets, and nowhere near the 3-or-more-flags limb. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is a different field and may not be substituted for the trailing-90-day figure; under POL-GEN-01 that counter, and every other profile field on this artifact (rating, acceptance_rate, lifetime_trips, cancellation_rate), is CONTEXT ONLY and can ground no finding against this driver.

evidence EV-DPROF-02834 · clauses POL-RD-06, POL-GEN-01

None of POL-RD-07's limbs (a) to (c) is met, so the trace is not impaired for policy purposes and the escalation route in POL-RD-10(3) is not open on this record; the excess must be decided on this trace as measured.

evidence EV-GPS-02834 · clauses POL-RD-07, POL-RD-10

kept The driver has no route-defence to run on this record and does not pretend otherwise. The chat log for the trip holds 0 messages, so POL-RD-04's rider-requested detour test has no instruction to test, no waypoint_hint to corroborate and no distance that can be excluded on that ground. Neither pickup_amended_at nor dropoff_amended_at is set and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null, so POL-RD-05 has no amended endpoint and no stored re-quote to apply. Vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not displace the booked optimal. The measured excess therefore stands as measured, and the dispute narrows to the remedy and to whether the money evidence is this trip's at all.

evidence EV-CHAT-02834, EV-TRIP-02834 · clauses POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-12

kept No traffic advisory covers this trip: EV-ADVIS-02834-01 is MISSING — status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, no payload — so POL-RD-03's exoneration cannot be run on this record and no closure-adjusted optimal route exists. The driver's counter-statement says only 'Followed navigation'; it asserts no queue, breakdown, closure or incident and cites no advisory identifier, so nothing in it seeks POL-RD-03 exoneration. An assertion of that kind, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, discharges nothing under POL-RD-08. The missing artifact is cited here for its absence only, and the driver asks the judge to decide nothing from it.

evidence EV-ADVIS-02834-01, EV-GPS-02834 · clauses POL-RD-03, POL-RD-08

kept The money at stake is bounded by what the rider put in issue. The rider's quantified claim is $6.00, while the POL-RD-02 arithmetic on this ledger gives charged_total 39.06 less recomputed_fare 31.438 = 7.622, which rounds UP to 7.65. POL-GEN-03 defines PARTIAL_REFUND as the return of PART of the contested amount and FULL_REFUND as the return of the WHOLE of it; a refund cannot be larger than the sum the rider actually contested, so the ceiling on the rider-filed claim here is $6.00, not $7.65, and the driver's exposure is at most that sum.

evidence EV-FARE-02834 · clauses POL-GEN-03, POL-RD-02

kept The fare breakdown does not carry this trip's identifier on its own face: the payload of EV-FARE-02834 records trip_id TRP-02734, while EV-TRIP-02834 and EV-GPS-02834 both record TRP-02834. POL-RD-08(a) makes matching trip identifiers across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown part of the rider's initial burden before any burden shifts, and POL-RD-10(2) forbids a final ruling and mandates escalation where those three do not all match. The pre-pass rating the artifact COMPLETE does not answer the point: POL-GEN-02(3) keeps schema-level assessment and policy-level assessment separate, and POL-RD-10(2) is a policy-level identifier test. On this record no refund should issue and the disputed sum should be held rather than paid out, with escalation naming POL-RD-10(2) as its trigger and a fare breakdown bearing this trip's identifier as what would resolve it.

The judge's explanation, verbatim

To both parties: this dispute cannot be finally decided on the record as it stands, so it goes to a human reviewer and the $6.00 in dispute is held — neither collected nor refunded. The reason is an identifier mismatch. The fare breakdown in the bundle, EV-FARE-02834, is indexed to this trip, but the ledger's own record inside it says "trip_id": "TRP-02734", while the trip record EV-TRIP-02834 and the GPS trace EV-GPS-02834 both say TRP-02834. POL-RD-10(2) requires the trip identifiers on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown to all match and forbids a final ruling where they do not. The pre-pass marking the artifact COMPLETE does not answer this: POL-GEN-02(3) keeps the schema-level assessment separate from the policy-level test, and this is a policy-level test. So the rider's assertion that all three artifacts bear TRP-02834 holds for the trip record and the trace but not for the fare breakdown. What would resolve the case is a fare breakdown or payment-ledger export for TRP-02834 — a corrected ledger line, or the gantry/payment record for this trip; the reviewer can call for it. The rest of the record, so the reviewer has it. The deviation itself is established but not material: the trace measures 30.94 km against the booked optimal 23.8 km, an excess of 7.14 km (30.0%), which passes the POL-RD-01 gates of 0.8 km and 20% but is below the 8.0 km and 50% materiality marks, so no POL-RD-06 uplift and no conduct referral is available (the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 326 completed trips in 90 days in any event). The trace is not impaired for policy purposes — 243 fixes at 10 seconds, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 seconds — so POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10(3) are not engaged. Nothing exonerates the excess: the chat log is empty (POL-RD-04 and POL-RD-14 have no instruction to test), no pickup or dropoff was amended and no amended optimal exists (POL-RD-05), the vehicle is RYDE_X so the pooled baseline of POL-RD-12 does not apply, and the only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-02834-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and the driver's 'Followed navigation' statement — which names no advisory and asserts no closure, queue or incident — discharges nothing under POL-RD-08. That absence does not itself escalate the case: under POL-RD-13 the missing advisory is a gap in the bundle, not the cited-artifact defect POL-RD-10(5) describes, because the driver cited no advisory at all. The fare is metered (fare_model METERED, quoted_fare_sgd null), so POL-RD-11 does not apply and the POL-RD-02 arithmetic would run as charged_total 39.06 less recomputed_fare 31.4380 = 7.6220, rounding up to 7.65 — above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, below the 90% full-refund share, and below the SGD 150.00 escalation ceiling. The driver's argument that any award is capped at the $6.00 contested, and the rider's contrary arithmetic of 7.65, are noted for the reviewer; no money moves now, because escalation under POL-RD-10 is terminal. No referral is issued: no clause produces one here (no POL-RD-06(c) pattern; no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity defect, the ERP and surcharge lines all being zero). Confidence is 0.85, capped by the weight-1.0 artifacts that carry the deciding identifier facts. The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
